sources.locator: §5.1 'Functors between module categories', printed pp.47–57 (Theorem 5.1.43 p.54; Proposition 5.1.40; Exercise 5.1.41; Proposition 5.1.44; Lemma 5.1.46; Corollary 5.1.48; Corollary 5.1.49); §5.2 'Morita equivalence', printed pp.57–58 inspected

contents.name: Categorical preliminaries: arbitrary (co)limits from (co)products and (co)kernels; additivity identifies (co)equalisers with (co)kernels
Proposition 5.1.40: the functor N⊗_R− preserves all colimits
Exercise 5.1.41: tensor–Hom correspondence between homomorphisms M⊗_R N → A and R-module maps N → Hom(M,A), with the S-linear variant
Proposition 5.1.44 and Lemma 5.1.46: a map of colimit-preserving functors is determined by its component at R, and the component being an isomorphism (or 0) propagates to every module
Theorem 5.1.43 (Eilenberg–Watts): F is isomorphic to F_N for some S⊗R°-module N if and only if F commutes with all colimits (equivalently, with all quotients and direct sums)
Corollary 5.1.48, first part: N ↦ F_N determines an equivalence from R–S-bimodules to colimit-preserving functors
Corollary 5.1.48, second part: composition of tensor functors corresponds to tensor product of bimodules (F_M ∘ F_N ≅ F_{M⊗_S N})
Corollary 5.1.49: the base-change functor F_S for a ring map is the tensor functor with kernel S, and its endomorphism ring is computed through that bimodule
§5.2 Morita equivalence: Definition 5.2.1, Corollary 5.2.2, Example 5.2.3
contents.reason: Morita equivalence of rings, invertible bimodules and the matrix-ring example belong to the Morita bicategories pair, which builds directly on this page.

sources.title: A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories (arXiv:0806.0832v1)
sources.locator: pp.1–8: Theorems 1.1–1.2 (p.1); §2.1–2.4 and Lemma 2.2 (p.4); §3, Theorem 3.1, Propositions 3.2–3.3, Lemma 3.4 (pp.4–8); §4 (pp.8–9) inspected for scope only

contents.name: Theorem 1.1 (Watts for arbitrary rings: right exact and direct-sum-preserving functors are tensoring with B = F(R))
Theorem 1.2: the functor Mod(R^° ⊗_Z S) → B(Mod_R, Mod_S) induced by B ↦ −⊗_R B is an equivalence of categories
Lemma 2.2: F(R) carries a ring homomorphism R → End_A(F R) (the bimodule structure from right multiplications)
Proposition 3.2: essential surjectivity of Ψ, via the unit at R, free modules through direct sums, and the canonical presentation of an arbitrary module as the cokernel of a map of free modules
Proposition 3.3: R⊗_R− is isomorphic to the identity functor on the recovered module category
§3.3–3.4 and Lemma 3.4: a natural transformation of right exact direct-sum-preserving functors is determined by its component at R (fullness and faithfulness of Ψ)
§4 application: right exact direct-sum-preserving functors on modules over an affine scheme are tensoring with a quasi-coherent sheaf
contents.reason: This pair treats modules over rings; the affine-scheme application needs the quasi-coherent sheaf and scheme machinery of the algebraic-geometry track and is not developed here.

sources.title: J. Fuchs, G. Schaumann, C. Schweigert, Eilenberg–Watts calculus for finite categories and a bimodule Radford S^4 theorem (arXiv:1612.04561v3)

contents.name: Introduction: classical Eilenberg–Watts statement for unital rings R,S — right exact functors preserving small coproducts are tensoring with an S-R-bimodule, with kernel F(R_R) carrying the natural right action
§2.1 Lemma 2.1: for finite-dimensional algebras, left exact ⇔ left adjoint ⇔ Hom_A(M,−), and right exact ⇔ right adjoint ⇔ G(A)⊗_A−
contents.reason: The finite-dimensional-algebra classification is the finite right/left exact form built by the finite abelian categories pair; this page keeps only the arbitrary-ring statement.

contents.name: §2.1 Lemma 2.2: Lex(A-mod,B-mod) ≃ (A-bimod-B)^op ≃ Rex(A-mod,B-mod) for finite-dimensional algebras
contents.reason: The Lex/Rex duality belongs to the finite pair's module duality and left exact variant, not to the arbitrary-ring theorem proved here.

contents.name: §3.2 Theorem 3.2 (categorical Eilenberg–Watts): Lex(A,B) ≃ A^op ⊞ B ≃ Rex(A,B) for finite k-linear categories
contents.reason: The categorical form uses Deligne products of finite linear categories, which the Deligne products pair constructs; this pair does not assume them.

contents.name: §3.5 Lemmas 3.15–3.16 and formulas (3.56)–(3.58): Nakayama and Serre adjunctions for finite linear categories
contents.reason: Nakayama functors come from the finite end/coend calculus built by the Deligne products pair; no Nakayama claim is made on this page.

contents.name: §1.8 Definitions 1.8.5–1.8.6: finite k-linear abelian categories as categories of finite-dimensional modules over finite-dimensional algebras
contents.reason: The intrinsic finite-category definition and its module-model characterization are the finite pair's subject, not this arbitrary-ring page.

contents.name: §1.8 Proposition 1.8.10: an additive k-linear functor A-mod → B-mod over finite-dimensional algebras is representable exactly when it is right exact; proof by the canonical free presentation and cokernel universality
§1.8 Corollary 1.8.11: an additive left exact functor from a finite abelian category to vector spaces is Hom_C(V,−)
contents.reason: The left exact representability result is the finite pair's left exact variant; this page proves only the right exact arbitrary-ring theorem.
